verses.text: So, holy brothers and sisters, you who share in God's call from heaven, think carefully about Jesus. He is the one God sent, and the High Priest of the faith we believe.
He was faithful to God, who chose him, just as Moses was faithful in all God's house.
But Jesus deserves more glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honour than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, but God is the one who built everything.
Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant. He told the people about things God would say in the future.
But Christ is faithful as the Son in charge of God's house. And we are his house, if we hold on firmly to our courage and to the hope we are proud of, right to the end.
That is why the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear his voice,
do not make your hearts stubborn, as your people did when they rebelled, on the day they tested God in the desert.
There your ancestors tested me and tried me, even though they saw what I did for forty years.
That is why I was angry with that generation. I said, 'Their hearts always go the wrong way. They have not known my ways.'
So in my anger I made a promise: 'They will never enter my place of rest.'"
Brothers and sisters, be careful that none of you has an evil heart that does not believe, and turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage each other every day, while it is still called "today", so that none of you is fooled by sin and becomes stubborn.
We share in Christ, if we hold on firmly to the trust we had at the beginning, right to the end.
As the Scripture says, "Today, if you hear his voice, do not make your hearts stubborn, as your people did when they rebelled."
Who heard God's voice and still rebelled? It was all those whom Moses led out of Egypt.
Who was God angry with for forty years? It was with those who sinned, and they died in the desert.
Who did God promise would never enter his place of rest? It was those who disobeyed him.
So we see that they could not enter because they did not believe.
